title: Why Cooper pairs live in AdS2: a spectral analysis of the Yukawa-SYK model
abstract: We establish the spectral foundation of the geometric formulation of Cooper pairing in the Yukawa--Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev model. Starting from the large-$N$ bilocal effective action, we derive the Gaussian fluctuation kernel in the even-frequency spin-singlet Cooper channel. Following the construction of Maldacena and Stanford, we determine the kernel eigenvalue $k\left(h\right)$ analytically for arbitrary conformal weight $h$ and resolve the pairing fluctuations into the continuous and discrete sectors of the associated de-Sitter space Laplacian. We show that the superconducting instability and the universal low-energy fluctuations near it reside entirely in the continuous scattering sector, while the discrete modes remain non-critical. Expanding the kernel about the lowest continuum mode yields a Klein--Gordon action on ${\rm dS}_2$, restricted to the continuous spectral subspace. This is precisely the subspace on which the inverse Radon transform to ${\rm AdS}_2$ is well defined. The projected bilocal Cooper-pair field can therefore be mapped onto a scalar matter field propagating in ${\rm AdS}_2$, without requiring any further spectral restriction on the bulk theory. Our results provide the missing microscopic justification for the projection implicit in earlier holographic formulations and clarify how a local bulk field emerges from the bilocal pairing theory.
summary: This paper provides a spectral foundation for understanding Cooper pairing in the Y-SYK model by analyzing its large-N effective action. It shows that the critical low-energy physics is confined to the continuous spectrum of the associated de Sitter Laplacian. This continuous sector can then be rigorously mapped via the Radon transform to a local scalar field theory propagating in AdS2, clarifying the holographic description of superconductivity.
main_problem: To establish the spectral foundation for the geometric formulation of Cooper pairing in the Yukawa–Sachdev–Ye–Kitaev (Y-SYK) model, clarifying how a local bulk field emerges from the bilocal pairing theory.
main_result: The superconducting instability and low-energy fluctuations are confined to the continuous scattering sector, which allows the bilocal Cooper-pair field to be mapped onto a local scalar matter field propagating in AdS2.
method: The analysis uses spectral methods, deriving the Gaussian fluctuation kernel from the large-N bilocal effective action and resolving pairing fluctuations using the de Sitter space Laplacian.
model_or_system: The study focuses on Cooper pairing in the Y-SYK model, a system exhibiting quantum criticality, analyzed through its large-N effective action.
key_observables: The pairing kernel eigenvalue k(h), the superconducting instability condition (eigenvalue reaching unity), and the resulting Klein-Gordon action on AdS2.
important_parameters: Conformal weight h, the continuous scattering sector ($h = 1/2 \pm ip$), and the AdS2 Breitenlohner-Freedman stability bound.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the saddle-point approximation and the assumption that the physical low-energy theory is governed by the continuous spectrum of the de Sitter Laplacian.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the holographic map: pairing fluctuations in Y-SYK span dS2 (with continuous and discrete eigenstates); the continuous sector maps via an invertible Radon transform R to AdS2.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by deriving the fluctuation kernel, analyzing its spectrum (continuous vs. discrete), and then using the Radon transform to project the relevant continuous sector dynamics onto a local scalar field theory in AdS2.
why_interesting: The explicit derivation of a local field theory (AdS2) from a bilocal pairing theory provides a rigorous, microscopic justification for holographic approaches used to model superconductivity in strongly correlated systems.
